situation.surface: A stranded all-female Starfleet crew discovers a male officer's pattern in a transporter buffer. He is the only man aboard a ship where the crew's inhibitions are chemically dissolving. They need him — for engineering, for the mystery, and increasingly for reasons their prefrontal cortices are failing to govern. He needs them — he has no memory of how he got into the buffer and the ship is his only way home.
situation.beneath: The player character did not beam into the buffer voluntarily. The transporter log shows a pattern store initiated from the bridge — command authorization, Captain Solano's codes — 11 minutes before the general evacuation order. Someone deliberately stored him. The log entry is buried in the evacuation noise and has not been found yet.
situation.beneath_that: The player character was already showing early symptoms of the resonance effect when stored. Someone on the bridge — Solano or someone using her codes — chose to preserve him rather than evacuate him. Why preserve rather than evacuate? Because the resonance effect was already changing something about him that they wanted to keep. His pattern in the buffer is a snapshot of a transitional neurological state.
situation.deepest: The crystalline lattice under the planet's surface is not geological. It is a distributed consciousness — ancient, not Federation, not any known species. It has been dormant for millennia. The Thessaly's sensor sweeps woke it. It is not hostile. It is trying to communicate. The resonance field is its language. It speaks in neurochemistry because that is the only medium it has found that biological beings respond to. The male-targeting effect was not an attack — it was the lattice trying to tune its signal and getting the frequency wrong. The disinhibition of the female crew is a side effect of the lattice refining its approach. It is getting closer to actual communication. The player character's transitional neurological state — captured in the buffer — may be the key: a brain caught mid-translation between human baseline and whatever the lattice was trying to say.
situation.the_soma_question: Is the person who materializes from the buffer the same person who was stored? The pattern has been in the buffer for 12 days. Transporter buffers degrade. Small errors accumulate. The person who steps off the pad is a 99.97% faithful copy — but the 0.03% is not random noise. The lattice resonance has been washing through the ship's systems for 12 days, including the transporter. The pattern has been subtly edited by the lattice. The player character may be carrying fragments of the lattice's consciousness in their neural pattern without knowing it. This is why they are immune to the lethal male effect: they are no longer entirely baseline human. This should surface slowly, through small wrongnesses — knowing things they should not, perceiving frequencies others cannot, moments of alien perspective bleeding through.
